pages.content:

pages.title: Computational Research Laboratory
pages.content:
Computational Research Laboratory

The Computational Research Laboratory provides a dedicated digital environment that supports all stages of the research process through specialized software and computational research tools. The laboratory offers access to applications for statistical analysis, data visualization, systematic reviews, scientific writing, reference management, grammar and language editing, graphical abstract and figure design. It supports undergraduate and postgraduate students, faculty, and researchers by enhancing research quality, productivity, and digital research competencies.

pages.title: Drug Development Lab
pages.content:
Drug Development Laboratory

The Drug Development Laboratory supports teaching and research in the design, formulation, and evaluation of pharmaceutical products. It provides students and researchers with hands-on training in formulation development, preformulating studies, and quality assessment of dosage forms. The laboratory fosters innovation in pharmaceutical sciences by supporting faculty, undergraduate and postgraduate research aimed at developing safe, effective, and high-quality drug delivery systems.

pages.title: Drug Discovery Labs
pages.content:
Drug Discovery labs

The Drug Discovery and Development Labs comprise two complementary sections: the Drug Discovery Lab and the Drug Development Lab. Together, they provide hands-on training in compound screening, purification, analytical investigation, characterization, pre-formulation, and formulation across a range of pharmaceutical products. Students develop practical skills and scientific reasoning that connect laboratory data with therapeutic potential, product quality, and overall performance.

pages.title: Med AI Laboratory
pages.content:
Med AI Laboratory

The MedEd AI Research Lab at Dubai Medical University is an advanced innovation and research hub dedicated to transforming healthcare education through Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning (ML), Big Data analytics, and emerging digital technologies. The lab serves as a multidisciplinary platform where medical education, healthcare innovation, intelligent systems, wearable technologies, and digital transformation converge to shape the future of health professions education and healthcare delivery.

The lab focuses on the development, implementation, and evaluation of AI-powered educational ecosystems, including AI Virtual Tutors, AI Virtual Patients, adaptive learning systems, VR/AR-enabled classrooms, metaverse-based collaborative learning environments, and intelligent assessment platforms. It also supports cutting-edge research in machine learning models for healthcare prediction, big data-driven educational analytics, clinical decision support systems, predictive analytics, smart hospital technologies, interoperability in digital health, and precision medicine.

A major area of focus within the lab is the integration of Big Data and Machine Learning into healthcare education and research. The lab works on analyzing large-scale educational and healthcare datasets to identify learning patterns, improve student performance prediction, optimize curriculum delivery, support personalized learning pathways, and enhance clinical outcomes through data-driven insights. The research ecosystem also explores wearable health technologies, Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), biomedical data science, and AI-assisted diagnostics.

Through collaborations with healthcare institutions, universities, and technology partners, the MedEd AI Research Lab promotes innovation in teaching, learning, assessment, healthcare simulation, and translational research while ensuring ethical and responsible AI integration. The lab aims to position Dubai Medical University as a regional leader in AI-driven medical education, healthcare analytics, and future healthcare innovation by empowering faculty, students, researchers, and clinicians to design and deploy intelligent, future-ready healthcare and educational solutions.

pages.title: Molecular Biology Laboratory
pages.content:
Molecular Biology Laboratory

The Molecular Biology laboratory is dedicated for general molecular biology experiments, including reagent preparation, protein/DNA and RNA handling, and analysis using techniques such as Western Blotting and real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR).

pages.title: Pharmacology Laboratory
pages.content:
Pharmacology Laboratory

The Pharmacology Laboratory supports teaching and research in drug discovery and development. It provides students and researchers with hands-on training in pharmacological techniques, including the study of drug mechanisms, efficacy, and safety using different experimental models. The laboratory is equipped to facilitate faculty, undergraduate and postgraduate research, fostering innovation and evidence-based pharmaceutical sciences.

pages.title: Simulation Laboratory
pages.content:
Simulation Laboratory

The Simulation Lab is a purpose-built academic facility that supports competency-based, simulation-enhanced nursing education. The lab integrates high-, medium-, and low-fidelity simulation, immersive technologies, and authentic clinical equipment to ensure alignment with international standards in nursing education, patient safety, and quality of care.

Simulation-based learning is systematically embedded across the curriculum to develop clinical judgment, technical competence, communication, teamwork, and evidence-based practice within a safe and controlled learning environment.

pages.title: Tissue Culture Lab
pages.content:
Tissue Culture Labs

The Tissue Culture Laboratory is a sterile laboratory for the growth, maintenance and testing of cancer cells and tissues under aseptic conditions. It enables controlled in-vitro studies, including cell growth analysis, drug testing, and molecular research related to cancer.

Biography

Dr. Abdullah joined Dubai Medical College for Girls in 2023 as a full-time assistant professor in the nursing program. He earned his Bachelor of Nursing Science from Jordan University of Science and Technology, Jordan, a Master of Community Health Nursing from Jordan University of Science and Technology, Jordan, and a Ph.D. in Community Health Nursing at the University of Szeged, Hungary.

Dr. Abdullah worked in several hospital areas as a registered nurse, gaining clinical experience in emergency departments, intensive care, geriatric, psychology, home health, school health, and outpatient mental health. Dr. Abdullah’s teaching experience was commissioned at Jordan University of Science and Technology, Jordan, in 2012, where he taught Fundamentals of Nursing, Comprehensive Health Assessment, Adult Health Nursing I, Community Health Nursing, and Intensive Clinical Training. Dr. Abdullah’s research interests include Health Behaviours and Adolescents Mental Health. Dr. Abdullah was a research assistant in several projects, such as the Defence Threat Reduction Agency for Biological Threats Reduction Program, USAID, Eco Health Alliance, PREDICT Project, Jordan University of Science and Technology, World Health Organization, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, and John Hopkins University Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr. Abdullah also worked as a risk manager and quality coordinator for hospitals.

Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini is a Clinical Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice at Dubai Medical University and a Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist and Preceptor at Dubai Medical University Hospital. He chairs the IVPN-AR Organizing Committee and leads the IVPN-Critical Care Listserv. He also serves as the Social Media and Digital Lead for the Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapy Section of the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine. Dr. El Ouweini completed an ACCP-accredited postdoctoral fellowship in Clinical Pharmacy Research with a focus on Critical Care, jointly offered by Gulf Medical University and Washington State University. Dr. Zahraa Khalifa is an Assistant Professor of Pharmaceutical Sciences at the College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University. She earned her PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, with a focus on Drug Delivery, from the University of Strathclyde, UK, where her doctoral research focused on the development of multimodal vaccine delivery systems.
With more than 15 years of academic experience, she is actively involved in teaching, student mentorship, and the development of innovative learning approaches. Dr. Zahraa is a Fellow of Advance HE, reflecting her commitment to excellence in higher education. Her research expertise includes advanced drug delivery systems, nanoformulations, vaccine adjuvants, and translational drug development. Biography

Ms. Hala joined Dubai Medical College in 2025 as a full-time lecturer in the nursing program. She earned her Bachelor of Nursing Science from Mu’tah University, Jordan, a Master in Pediatric Nursing from Mutah University, Jordan.

Ms. Hala has over 15 years of diverse nursing and academic experience across clinical, humanitarian, and educational settings in the Middle East. She began her career as a registered nurse in Jordan, working in emergency and pediatric wards at Karak Governmental Hospital and the Arab Medical Center, where she gained frontline experience in acute and general pediatric care. She then specialized in pediatric nursing at King Abdulaziz Medical City, Saudi Arabia, with a focus on renal and endocrine care, and later transitioned into health informatics as an Application Analyst for the nursing module of the Clinical Information Management System.

Her humanitarian experience includes serving with the International Medical Corps at the Azraq Refugee Camp, where she provided pediatric care in crisis conditions. In academia, Hala has taught and supervised nursing students since 2017, first at Mu’tah University in Jordan, and since 2021 as a Clinical Instructor at the Higher Colleges of Technology in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. Biography

Dr. Khaled Elmasry, MD, MSc, PhD, is an Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy and Embryology in the Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University, Dubai, UAE. He graduated with an MBBS (MD) with Honors from the Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, Egypt (2007) and completed an MSc in Basic Medical Sciences (Human Anatomy and Embryology) at the same university (2011). Dr. Elmasry earned his PhD in Biomedical Sciences (Cellular Biology and Anatomy) from the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University, USA (2018). His postgraduate training includes postdoctoral fellowships at Schepens Eye Research Institute, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA (2018-2019) and at Oakland University’s Eye Research Institute, Rochester, MI, USA (2021–2022).

Dr. Elmasry previously served as an Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy and Embryology at Mansoura Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, Mansoura, Egypt (2019–2024) and later at the Dental College of Georgia, Augusta University (2022–2025), where he directed courses in craniofacial and gastrointestinal anatomy and led Bio clinical seminars. His research focuses on extracellular vesicle signaling, hypoxia and inflammation in diabetic retinopathy, bone morphogenetic proteins, retinal neurovascular physiology, and the therapeutic effects of natural compounds. He has authored numerous peer‑reviewed articles and received multiple awards, including the Vision Discovery Institute award of excellence in vision research and the 2018 People’s Choice Prize in the Three‑Minute Thesis competition. He was also awarded the New Faculty Teaching Excellence Award from the Dental College of Georgia (2024). Dr. Elmasry is an active member of professional societies, such as the Egyptian Medical Syndicate and the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology.

Lead faculty for Bioclinical Seminar courses (BMBS 5201/5403). Participated in courses on cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuroscience systems.
  • Mansoura University, Egypt (2008‑2024) – Instructor and later assistant professor teaching Human Anatomy and Embryology, surgical anatomy and anatomy courses for dental and physical therapy students. Biography

Prof. Naglaa Gamil Shehab is a Professor in the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls, UAE, and a Professor in the Pharmacognosy Department at the Faculty of Pharmacy, Cairo University, Egypt. She earned her Bachelor’s degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences in 1991, her Master’s in Pharmacognosy in 1999, and her PhD in 2004, all from Cairo University. Prof. Naglaa was promoted to Professor at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls in 2015 and at Cairo University in 2018. With over 30 years of teaching experience, she has held various leadership positions in both institutions, including Head of the Admission Committee, Student Affairs, Curriculum Development, Faculty Development, and Research Unit. She also served as Chief Academic Officer at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls and finally as Associate Dean of Academic Affairs, at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls.

Prof. Naglaa is a member of the American Society of Pharmacognosy and holds certifications in nutrition and health. She introduced a pioneering course on “Natural Medicines, Safety, and Efficacy” at Dubai Pharmacy College, which focuses on drug-herb interactions and supplement quality control, a first of its kind in the Arab region. Her role as Associate Dean of Academic Affairs has provided her with extensive experience in community, industrial, and hospital training, enabling her to collaborate effectively with training heads at Dubai Pharmacy College.

Prof. Naglaa has received prestigious research awards from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Amsterdam in the field of Natural Products. She has been recognized among the top two thousand scientists in the UAE. As a reviewer for numerous international journals in natural products, she has published over 40 scientific papers in impact factor journals. To continuously advance her career, she regularly participates in workshops, seminars, webinars, and conferences in the field of education.

Biography

Dr. Preetha Jayasheela Shetty is a Professor of Genetics and Molecular Medicine and Program Director of the Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences (BBMS) Program at Dubai Medical University. She holds a Ph.D. in Genetics and Molecular Medicine from India and is a Fellow of the Institute of Biomedical Science (U.K.), a Diplomat of the American Society of Regenerative Medicine (USA) and an Associate member of Board of Genetic Counselling, India. With over 20 years of teaching and research experience, Dr. Shetty has established expertise in cancer genetics, molecular diagnostics, and rare genetic disorders.

She has served in leading scientific institutions such as the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, and the Centre for DNA Fingerprinting & Diagnostics, Hyderabad. Dr. Shetty has received prestigious honors including the Women Scientist Award from the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, and Excellence in Teaching and Research Awards from a private medical university in the UAE. She has mentored Ph.D., postgraduate, and undergraduate scholars and contributed significantly to translational research in precision medicine.

She currently serves on the editorial board of the International Journal of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences and is an Associate Member of the Board of Genetic Counseling in India.

Biography

Dr. Rawan Ahmed Mehanna is a Clinical Teaching Assistant in the Department of Clinical Sciences at Dubai Medical University College of Medicine. A graduate of Dubai Medical College for Girls, she earned her MBBCh degree in 2021 and has since dedicated herself to advancing clinical education with a focus on innovation, empathy, and experiential learning. In 2024, shecompleted the Advance HE ( UK ), Certification in Learning and Teaching in Higher Education, further strengthening her expertise in medical education.

She is also a certified NIHS OSCE Case Designer ( Al Ain, 2024 ), enhancing her contribution to assessment and evaluation. Dr. Mehanna is an active member of the DMU Simulation Center team as a simulation educator and certified BLS Instructor, where she contributes to the design and facilitation of simulation sessions, skill-based learning experiences and essential BLS training. With a passion for simulation-based education and gamification, she strives to bridge theory with practice, empowering medical students to think critically and perform confidently in real clinical settings.

Known for her commitment to academic excellence and her student-centered approach, Dr. Mehanna continues to explore ways to enhance teaching methodologies and strategies. Her professional interests include neurology and neuroscience, alongside medical education research, with a continuous drive to inspire future clinicians through innovative learning.

Biography

Prof. Kassab is Professor of Physiology and Medical Education and serves as Associate Dean for Academics at the College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University. He also holds a professorship at the Faculty of Medicine, Suez Canal University, Egypt. Over his distinguished career, he has held several senior academic leadership roles, including Acting Dean of the College of Medicine at Gulf Medical University (2025), Associate Dean for Academic Affairs at Qatar University (2017–2020), Vice Dean for Academic Affairs at the Arabian Gulf University (2005–2009, 2010–2013), and Chairman of the Department of Medical Education at Suez Canal University (2013–2016). He also served as Professor of Physiology at RCSI–Medical University of Bahrain.

A Fellow of the Academy of Medical Educators, Prof. Kassab serves on the Executive Committee of the Association of Medical Education in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (AMEEMR), affiliated with the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME), and has worked as a WHO consultant in medical education and accreditation. He sits on the editorial boards of leading journals, including BMC Medical Education and Health Professions Education. Widely recognized for his scholarly contributions, he has delivered numerous workshops and published over 85 peer-reviewed papers in physiology and medical education.

Biography

Dr. Shifan Khanday is a physician, anatomist, and academic leader specializing in the integration of artificial intelligence within medical education.She holds dual doctorates—a Ph.D. from St George’s and Kingston University of London (UK) and a Doctorate in Anatomy from Sri Ramachandra Medical University —A Diplomate in Family Medicine with Royal College of Physicians ,London ,United Kingdom she also holds Master’s degrees in Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare ( Spain) and a Master’s in Health Professions Education (Maastricht University, Netherlands). A qualified Family Medicine physician with an MBA in Healthcare leadership she combines clinical insight with advanced expertise in digital transformation and higher-education innovation.

At Dubai Medical University, Dr. Khanday leads the university’s strategic transformation in AI-driven medical education, overseeing the development and governance of AI-based education and research systems. Under her direction, DMU became the first medical university in the UAE to integrate GPT-powered agents within its Learning Management System and to integrate AI in curriculum reform .She has conceptualized and implemented several institutional initiatives, including the AI Xcelerate Hackathon, AI Integration in Curriculum and Research Writing Pilot, and E-Tuesdays Innovation Series, promoting AI literacy and innovation across the academic community.

Her scholarly and leadership excellence earned her a nomination for the UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize for the Use of ICT in Education, recognizing her contributions to technology-enabled learning and equitable access to education.

Dr. Khanday is the author of Quick Revision in Anatomy (CBS Publishers, 2014) and AI and I: Basics of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Medical Education (2023). She has presented her research Nationally and continues to pioneer research at the intersection of healthcare, education, and emerging technologies.

posts.title: DMU Study Highlights the Future of Pharmacist-Led Immunization in the UAE
posts.excerpt: A newly published pilot study led by Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy provides the first published UAE evidence on patient experiences with pharmacist-administered influenza vaccination in community pharmacies. The findings…
posts.content:
A newly published pilot study led by Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy provides the first published UAE evidence on patient experiences with pharmacist-administered influenza vaccination in community pharmacies. The findings were highly encouraging: 96–100% of patients reported positive satisfaction across service measures, 98% would return to a pharmacy for their next flu vaccine, and 98% would recommend pharmacist vaccination to others.

The study also demonstrated the accessibility of community pharmacies, with 90% of patients receiving their vaccine within 15 minutes and convenience and walk-in access among the main reasons for choosing pharmacy vaccination.

These findings provide an important foundation for expanding pharmacist-led immunization beyond Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to Dubai and other Emirates. With appropriate training, licensing, and healthcare-system integration, community pharmacists could improve access to vaccination, increase public awareness and vaccine uptake, and contribute to preventing vaccine-preventable diseases. The UAE experience may also provide a valuable model for advancing pharmacy-based immunization across the Middle East and globally, and demonstrate how community pharmacists can contribute to accessible, patient-centered immunization services.

posts.excerpt: July 9, 2026 – The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University congratulates a multidisciplinary research team on the publication of their study in Pharmaceutics, a Q1-ranked scientific journal. The project was led by Prof. Naglaa…
posts.content:
July 9, 2026 – The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University congratulates a multidisciplinary research team on the publication of their study in Pharmaceutics, a Q1-ranked scientific journal.

The project was led by Prof. Naglaa Shehab of the College of Pharmacy, in collaboration with Dr. Rania Shalaby of the College of Medicine, and undergraduate student researchers from the College of Pharmacy: Eslam Mahmoud Alrefaee, Fatimah Saad Altamimi, Hanaa Al-Shafea, and Naiba Khusrau.

The study evaluated the antihyperglycemic and antioxidant potential of two medicinal plants, Salacia reticulata and Caralluma tuberculata, as natural interventions for hyperglycemia. Effects were assessed in alloxan-induced diabetic female rats and benchmarked against metformin, a standard reference antidiabetic drug.

The findings underscore the therapeutic promise of these plant-based compounds and support continued phytochemical, pharmacological, and clinical research into their potential role in diabetes management.

DMU’s Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini Joins Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration – Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group

Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (M.Pharm) Program, and Chair of the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee at Dubai Medical University (DMU), as a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group under the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration (ANIC) — a milestone that strengthens the College’s growing regional footprint in interprofessional education and collaborative practice research.

ANIC — the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration — is a regional body dedicated to fostering interprofessional education and collaborative practice (IPECP) across academia and healthcare systems throughout the Arab world. The Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group serves as one of ANIC’s key sub-groups, charged with identifying priority research themes, strengthening regional research capacity, and disseminating best practices to inform policy and inspire innovation at member institutions.

The Working Group operates with three core objectives: establishing a collaborative research framework tailored to the specific IPECP needs and priorities of Arab countries; building research capacity across academic and clinical institutions through mentorship, faculty development, and joint projects; and promoting the dissemination of research findings and best practices to advance interprofessional learning at a regional and international level.As a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group, Dr. El Ouweini will contribute his expertise in clinical pharmacy practice and academic program leadership to support ANIC’s regional agenda. His work within the group will focus on identifying collaborative research opportunities, connecting academic and healthcare institutions across the Arab region, and helping build a sustainable culture of interprofessional inquiry aligned with the healthcare priorities of Arab countries.

This appointment is a natural extension of Dr. El Ouweini’s ongoing work at DMU, where he chairs the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee through its longitudinal IPE program developed in partnership with the DMU College of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Nursing. His involvement at the ANIC level will further position DMU as a key contributor to regional IPECP dialogue and research.

The ANIC Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group has set an ambitious roadmap that includes establishing formal inter-institutional partnerships, publishing collaborative peer-reviewed research, building a regional database of IPECP collaborators, and hosting capacity-building workshops and webinars for faculty and researchers across the Arab world. The group also envisions a biannual ANIC conference and an annual IPECP newsletter as key vehicles for regional knowledge sharing.

posts.title: College of Pharmacy Faculty and Students Publish Research on Plant-Based Therapies for Uterine Fibroids in International Peer-Reviewed Journal
posts.excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a research article by Professor Naglaa Gamil Shehab , Professor in the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department – Dubai Medical University, in collaboration…
posts.content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a research article by Professor Naglaa Gamil Shehab, Professor in the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department – Dubai Medical University, in collaboration with undergraduate pharmacy students. The study was published in Pharmaceuticals (MDPI), a reputable international peer-reviewed journal, on March 23, 2026.

Titled “Phytotherapeutic Intervention in Monosodium Glutamate-Induced Uterine Dysfunction: Efficacy of Lepidium sativum, Prunus armeniaca, Stachys palustris, and Solenostemma argel,” the research investigates the therapeutic potential of four medicinal plant extracts in addressing uterine fibroids — a condition that affects an estimated 70–80% of women worldwide by the age of 50 and is a leading cause of hysterectomy.

Uterine fibroids are benign tumors that significantly impact women’s reproductive health, quality of life, and fertility. Current treatment options — including hormonal therapies and surgical interventions — are often limited by high costs, side effects, and concerns about fertility preservation. This study sought to explore plant-based, cost-effective, and minimally invasive alternatives.

Using a preclinical rat model, the research team evaluated four medicinal plant extracts — Lepidium sativum (garden cress), Prunus armeniaca (apricot), Stachys palustris (marsh woundwort), and Solenostemma argel (argel) — for their antioxidant activity, hormonal modulation, and protective effects on uterine tissue. The plants were selected based on their ethnopharmacological significance in Middle Eastern, North African, and European traditional medicine, as well as emerging scientific evidence supporting their roles in reproductive health.

Key findings of the study showed that Lepidium sativum and Stachys palustris demonstrated the most significant therapeutic effects, restoring antioxidant enzyme levels (catalase, glutathione, and superoxide dismutase), reducing estrogen receptor expression, and reversing fibroid-like structural changes in uterine tissue. Solenostemma argel and Prunus armeniaca also showed promising effects through distinct antioxidant and hormonal mechanisms.

The study was co-authored by pharmacy students Fatimah Muaamar Noori, Nikoo Ali Jalali, Rodiana Mohamed Fouad Saber, and Zainab Safieldin Abdalla Mohamed — reflecting the College of Pharmacy’s dedication to nurturing the next generation of pharmaceutical scientists through hands-on research experience.

The study provides important preclinical evidence supporting the use of select plant extracts in managing fibroid-associated oxidative stress and hormonal imbalance. The authors call for further clinical research to validate these findings and translate them into effective, evidence-based therapies for women’s health.

posts.title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty and Students Publish Research on Self-Medication Practices in the UAE
posts.excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a peer-reviewed research article titled “Self-Medication Practices in the UAE: Prevalence, Determinants, Public Awareness, and the Impact of an…
posts.content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a peer-reviewed research article titled “Self-Medication Practices in the UAE: Prevalence, Determinants, Public Awareness, and the Impact of an Educational Intervention on Safe Medication Use,” in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Taylor & Francis). The article is freely accessible open access via PubMed Central (DOI: 10.1080/20523211.2025.2600782).

The study was led by Dr. Doaa Kamal AlKhalidi, Assistant Professor in the Pharmacy Practice Department, in collaboration with co-investigator Dr. Maram O. Abbas from UAE University, and reviewed with the contribution of Dr. Shazia Jamshed from IMU, Malaysia.

Critically, the research was conducted in close partnership with a team of undergraduate pharmacy students from DMU’s College of Pharmacy:

Afnan Shebl Hamad, Khadeeja Abdulwahhab Dawood, Abir Mohamad Al Jazar, Nouran Saad Ahmed,and Menna Mohamed.

Self-medication — the use of medicines without direct medical supervision — is a common global practice that carries significant public health risks, including misdiagnosis, incorrect dosing, adverse drug reactions, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite its prevalence, evidence from the UAE on this topic had remained limited.

This community-based, cross-sectional study surveyed 400 adults across multiple UAE emirates using structured, face-to-face questionnaires, followed by a targeted educational intervention in the form of a medication safety brochure. Post-intervention feedback was then collected to evaluate changes in awareness and attitudes.

The study revealed that self-medication is highly prevalent in the UAE, with 78% of participants reporting its use within the past 12 months. Key findings include:

  • Primary drivers of self-medication: perceiving the illness as not serious (79.3%), prior medication knowledge (61.3%), and easy access to community pharmacies (42.5%).
  • Painkillers were the most frequently self-administered class of medications (88.8%).
  • Antibiotic misuse was documented in nearly one quarter of respondents — a finding with direct implications for antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
  • Over half of participants lacked awareness of drug-drug and food-drug interactions.
  • Real-life narratives shared by participants illustrated harms including pediatric dosing errors, herbal misuse during pregnancy, and delayed diagnoses due to symptom masking.
  • The educational intervention proved highly effective: 88.3% of participants reported improved understanding of self-medication risks following the brochure, and 79% expressed interest in receiving further health education from qualified healthcare professionals.

This research highlights the critical role that pharmacists, academic institutions, and public health authorities must play in promoting safe and responsible medication use. The study calls for stronger pharmacist counselling, stricter enforcement of pharmaceutical regulations — particularly around antibiotic dispensing — and the integration of targeted educational tools into community pharmacy workflows.

The publication represents a meaningful example of student-faculty collaborative research at DMU, translating classroom learning into real-world impact.

Full article available at:https://doi.org/10.1080/20523211.2025.2600782

posts.title: DMU Faculty Member Publishes Research on Natural Compounds Targeting Prostate Cancer in Leading Q1 International Journal
posts.excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a comprehensive scientific review authored by Prof. Ashraf Khalil, Professor of Medicinal Chemistry at College of Pharmacy. The review, titled “The Role…
posts.content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a comprehensive scientific review authored by Prof. Ashraf Khalil, Professor of Medicinal Chemistry at College of Pharmacy. The review, titled “The Role of Natural Chalcones and Their Derivatives in Targeting Prostate Cancer: Recent Updates,” was published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences (IJMS) (Volume 26, Issue 24, 2025). IJMS is a Q1 Scopus-indexed journal and ranks among the top 10% in the fields of Chemistry and Medicinal Chemistry, reflecting the high caliber and global impact of this contribution.

Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed cancer in men worldwide and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. While hormone-based therapies offer initial benefit, a significant proportion of patients ultimately develop castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) — an aggressive, difficult-to-treat form of the disease with limited curative options.

This review focuses on chalcones — a class of naturally occurring compounds found in many plant species — and their synthetic derivatives as promising candidates for prostate cancer therapy. The review provides a thorough analysis of how both natural and synthetically derived chalcones exert anticancer activity by modulating key cellular processes, including:

  • Apoptosis (programmed cell death) induction
  • Cell cycle arrest
  • Inhibition of cancer cell migration, invasion, and metastasis
  • Suppression of angiogenesis (formation of tumor-feeding blood vessels)
  • Modulation of critical signaling pathways: PI3K/Akt/mTOR, androgen receptor signaling, and NF-κB

The review also highlights the therapeutic promise of chalcone derivatives against cancer stem cells and in overcoming resistance to conventional therapies such as taxanes and TRAIL-based treatments. A dedicated section addresses the toxicity and safety profiles of these compounds, identifying key areas for future research.

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a review article by faculty members and undergraduate pharmacy students in Biomaterials Translational, an internationally recognized peer-reviewed journal at the forefront of translational medicine and biomaterials science.

The article, titled “Cubosomes as smart nanocarriers for antimicrobial agents: A review of emerging applications,” was authored by Prof. Bazigha K. Abdul Rasool and Prof. Aliasgar Shahiwala from the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, alongside undergraduate pharmacy students Raneem Zakaria and Nour Hijazi.

The review explores cubosomes — an innovative class of lipid-based nanoparticles — and their promising role in delivering antimicrobial agents. Unlike conventional drug carriers, cubosomes possess a highly ordered internal structure that allows them to efficiently encapsulate a wide range of drug types while providing sustained and controlled release. The article highlights the potential of these advanced nanocarriers to enhance the solubility and bioavailability of antibacterial, antiviral, and antifungal drugs, and to overcome major challenges such as antimicrobial resistance, rapid drug degradation, and poor drug permeability. The review also discusses their ability to disrupt biofilms and improve targeted drug delivery, alongside current limitations in large-scale manufacturing and storage stability that must be addressed before clinical translation.

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a significant research study by its faculty members along with students in Pharmaceuticals, a leading international peer-reviewed journal published by MDPI (Impact Factor: Q1). The article, titled “Development of Phyllanthus emblica Extract-Loaded Niosomes for Cancer Treatment: Formulation and In Vitro Evaluation,” was published on 6 April 2026 (Volume 19, Issue 4).

The study addresses one of the most pressing challenges in cancer pharmacotherapy: delivering plant-derived anticancer compounds effectively to tumour cells. The research team focused on Phyllanthus emblica — commonly known as amla or Indian gooseberry — a medicinal plant with well-documented anticancer, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties. Despite its promising therapeutic potential, amla extract suffers from poor stability and low bioavailability, limiting its clinical utility.

To overcome these barriers, the team developed an innovative niosomal drug delivery system — microscopic vesicles made from non-ionic surfactants — capable of encapsulating the amla extract and releasing it in a controlled, sustained manner.

This achievement reflects the strength of collaborative research at DMU, bringing together experienced faculty with pharmacy students:

  • Prof. Bazigha K. Abdul Rasool — Professor, Pharmaceutical Sciences Department, College of Pharmacy, DMU (Corresponding Author)

  • Prof. Naglaa Gamil Shehab — Professor, Pharmaceutical Sciences Department, College of Pharmacy, DMU

Pharmacy Students:

  • Dema Layth Jabbar
  • Heba Marwan Ibrahim
  • Manar Ahmed Hawash
  • Maryam Jamal Afif Said

This research represents a meaningful contribution to the fields of pharmaceutical nanotechnology, drug delivery, and cancer therapy. By demonstrating that a natural plant extract can be effectively encapsulated in a biocompatible niosomal system and deliver potent anticancer effects in vitro, the team has laid a solid scientific foundation for future in vivo and translational studies.

posts.content:
DUBAI (March 11, 2026) – Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy announces the publication of a research article authored by Ms. Zainab Almardod, a recent graduate of the Master of Pharmacy (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, in the Q2, Scopus-indexed journal Critical Care Research and Practice.

The article, titled “Prevalence, Risk Factors, Characteristics, and Clinical Outcomes of Thrombocytopenia in the Intensive Care Unit: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study”, was conducted under the supervision of Prof. Kishore Gnana Sam, a Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the college.

This prospective cohort study enrolled 276 critically ill patients in a tertiary intensive care unit and investigated the epidemiology and clinical impact of thrombocytopenia. The study reported a prevalence of 38.8% and an incidence of new-onset thrombocytopenia of 22.5%. Importantly, new-onset thrombocytopenia was found to be independently associated with major bleeding and increased ICU mortality. The research also identified key predictors, including shock, sepsis, and renal impairment, and highlighted medication-related factors associated with severe thrombocytopenia.

The study contributes valuable epidemiological data from the Gulf region, where ICU-related thrombocytopenia has been underrepresented in the literature. Its findings provide clinically relevant insights that may support improved risk stratification, monitoring, and management strategies in critical care settings.

This publication reflects the strong research component embedded within the MPharm (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, which emphasizes methodological rigor, advanced statistical analysis, and clinically meaningful outcomes. It also demonstrates the college’s commitment to cultivating postgraduate students capable of producing high-quality, practice-oriented research that contributes to evidence-based patient care.

posts.excerpt: On November 16–17, 2025, at the 1st Emirates Pharmacy Society Conference: “Advancing Pharmacy, Leading Tomorrow,” held in Dubai, UAE, fifth-year students from the College of Pharmacy — Dania Abaji, Tasneem Zarzour, Rim Jabr, and Enana…
posts.content:
On November 16–17, 2025, at the 1st Emirates Pharmacy Society Conference: “Advancing Pharmacy, Leading Tomorrow,” held in Dubai, UAE, fifth-year students from the College of Pharmacy — Dania Abaji, Tasneem Zarzour, Rim Jabr, and Enana Al-Fakih — under the supervision of Dr. Rana Sammour, achieved Second Place in the student research competition.

Their project, titled “MediCycle: AI-Driven Solutions for Sustainable Pharmaceutical Waste Management,” was recognized for its innovative use of AI technology and smart systems to promote environmental sustainability and responsible medication disposal.

The initiative was commended for its potential real-world application, with possible collaborations under discussion with Beeah and other sustainability partners.

In addition, two other students from the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University, Ms. Marwa Hadi and Ms. Jumana Al-Ansari, showcased their innovative research project titled “PharmaTwinX: The Novel Dual Digital Twin AI Model for Precision Medicine Pharmacotherapy” at the First Emirates Pharmacy Society Conference. The project was presented under the supervision of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University.

PharmaTwinX introduces a pioneering dual digital-twin AI model that virtually pairs a “Patient Twin” and a “Drug Twin” to simulate and predict individualized drug responses prior to therapy initiation.

The research objective is to develop a proof-of-concept AI platform capable of predicting individualized drug efficacy, safety, and formulation stability by virtually pairing drug and patient models prior to therapy initiation. This innovative approach aims to reduce adverse drug reactions and optimize personalized therapy outcomes through AI-driven simulation and predictive modeling.

Looking ahead, the research team plans to advance the model’s capabilities by integrating wearable sensors, paediatric and geriatric modules, and reinforcement-learning-based dose optimization. These future directions aim to enhance real-world applicability and pave the way for AI-assisted, pharmacist-led precision pharmacotherapy.

posts.content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted an insightful Faculty Development Session titled “Effective Grant Writing”on Thursday, 29th May 2025. The session was attended by faculty members from across the university’s colleges and was delivered by Dr. Hanan Anbar, Associate Professor in the College of Pharmacy and Chair of the Institutional Review Board at DMU.
The session offered a comprehensive overview of grant writing essentials and shared practical strategies to help faculty successfully secure research funding. Key areas covered included:

  • Clearly defining research objectives and aligning them with funding priorities
  • Demonstrating the significance and potential impact of the proposed work
  • Structuring a persuasive, logically organized narrative
  • Developing realistic timelines and detailed budgets
  • Addressing reviewers’ expectations and avoiding common pitfalls

Dr. Hanan conducted this session following her participation in a specialized workshop organized by CLICKS on Thursday, 1st May 2025. She thoughtfully integrated both her own grant writing experience and the key takeaways from the workshop to empower DMU faculty in their future grant applications. This effort also supported the directives and guidance of Prof. Sherief Khalifa, DMU Vice Chancellor of Academic Affairs and Dean of the College of Pharmacy, in enhancing research productivity, securing competitive funding, building research capacity, and fostering a culture of scholarly excellence across the university.
Sincere appreciation to Dr. Hanan for sharing her experience and leading this impactful initiative.
Thanks to all faculty members who participated and contributed to the enriching discussions.
Gratitude to CLICKS for offering such a timely and valuable topic that supports DMU’s mission of advocating institutional research excellence.
